references.text: Jesus declares that salvation has come to Zacchaeus' house. The concept of "salvation" (σωτηρία) linked to a specific house and a specific person shows that Jesus' mission was to bring salvation to individuals, cf. [ref:Luk 19:10|Luke 19:10] where Jesus says he came to seek and save the lost.

Jesus refers to a bent woman as "a daughter of Abraham" who had been bound by Satan for eighteen years. The parallel to [ref:Luk 19:9|Luke 19:9] is clear: Jesus identifies both as children of Abraham who have a right to God's salvation and deliverance ([ref:Luk 13:16|Luke 13:16]).

Direct continuation of the verse, where Jesus explains his mission: "For the Son of Man came to seek and save the lost" ([ref:Luk 19:10|Luke 19:10]). This provides the reason why salvation came to Zacchaeus' house.

God's promise to Abraham: "In you all the families of the earth shall be blessed" ([ref:1 Mos 12:3|Genesis 12:3]). Jesus' statement that Zacchaeus is "a son of Abraham" links salvation back to the covenant promise given to Abraham.

God establishes his covenant with Abraham and his offspring as an everlasting covenant ([ref:1 Mos 17:7-8|Genesis 17:7-8]). That Jesus calls Zacchaeus "a son of Abraham" points to this covenant belonging as the basis for salvation.

Paul writes: "So you see that it is those who have faith who are the children of Abraham" ([ref:Gal 3:7|Galatians 3:7]). Zacchaeus showed his faith through repentance and action, and Jesus recognizes him as a true son of Abraham.

"If you belong to Christ, then you are Abraham's offspring and heirs according to the promise" ([ref:Gal 3:29|Galatians 3:29]). Zacchaeus' identity as Abraham's son is tied to his faith and belonging, not merely physical descent.

Paul explains that the promise applies to "the whole offspring who have the faith of Abraham" ([ref:Rom 4:16|Romans 4:16]). Zacchaeus' repentance and faith are what make him a true son of Abraham in Jesus' eyes.

John the Baptist warns against relying on physical descent from Abraham: "Do not begin to say to yourselves, We have Abraham as our father" ([ref:Luk 3:8|Luke 3:8]). In contrast, Jesus identifies Zacchaeus as a true son of Abraham because he showed the fruit of repentance.

Paul says to the jailer: "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you will be saved, you and your household" ([ref:Apg 16:31|Acts 16:31]). The salvation that comes to an entire household is a parallel to Jesus' words that salvation came to Zacchaeus' house.

Isaiah proclaims: "My salvation is near, it will come soon" ([ref:Jes 56:1|Isaiah 56:1]). Jesus' words "Today salvation has come to this house" are a fulfillment of the prophetic promise that God's salvation comes near to people.

The Lord says: "I will seek the lost, I will bring back the driven away" ([ref:Esek 34:16|Ezekiel 34:16]). Jesus as the good shepherd seeks out Zacchaeus, the tax collector who was an outcast, and brings salvation to his house.
